definitions.explanation: A deep, dark shade of blue. One of the traditional Japanese colors, historically associated with indigo dyeing. Commonly used for school uniforms and business attire in Japan.

examples.japanese: {紺色|こんいろ}のスーツを{着|き}ている。
examples.english: I'm wearing a navy blue suit.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{制服|せいふく}は{紺色|こんいろ}だった。
examples.english: The school uniform was navy blue.

examples.japanese: {紺色|こんいろ}は{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}もフォーマルな{色|いろ}のひとつとされている。
examples.english: Navy blue is considered one of the most formal colors in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
Can function as a no-adjective: {紺色|こんいろ}の + noun. Often shortened to {紺|こん} in casual speech or compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紺色|こんいろ}のスーツ: navy blue suit
- {紺色|こんいろ}の{制服|せいふく}: navy blue uniform
- {濃|こ}い{紺色|こんいろ}: deep navy blue

CULTURAL NOTE:
{紺色|こんいろ} is one of the traditional Japanese colors ({和色|わしょく}), produced through repeated indigo ({藍|あい}) dyeing. It has long been a popular color in Japan and is sometimes called "{紺|こん}は{藍|あい}より{出|い}でて{藍|あい}より{青|あお}し," a proverb meaning the student surpasses the master.
